322013.title: The locally conical reflection arrangement conjecture
322013.statement:
Let $W$ be a well-generated reflection group acting on a complex vector space $V$. A generating set $R$ is **well-generating** when it generates $W$ and has cardinality $\dim V$. The system $(W,R)$ is called **abstractly locally conical** if, for every $U,T\subseteq R$ with $U$ nonempty, every Quillen fiber of

$$
\mathrm{Supp}:\mathrm{Face}(\Delta^U_T)\to \Pi^U_T\setminus\{\hat{1}\}
$$

has a cone point. **The locally conical reflection arrangement conjecture.** For each well-generated reflection group $W$, there exists a well-generating $R$ for which $(W,R)$ is abstractly locally conical. This property would provide the local conical structure needed to compare the relevant simplicial complexes with the intersection lattice of the reflection arrangement; whether every well-generated reflection group admits such a generating set is left open.
322013.review_depth: v2 Conjecture 12.8; v3 Conjecture 13.8 and preceding fixed-space definitions; v1 introduction; author PDF Quillen-fiber definition and cone lemma
322013.ordinary_attempt: Tried the common-vertex criterion on fixed-space fibers. A cone vertex must belong to every maximal face of the fiber, not merely make its order complex contractible. The source already treats Coxeter and Shephard systems. A bad fiber for one generating set cannot refute the existential quantifier on R.
322013.remaining_gap: Need either a new uniform choice of R for the remaining groups or a specific W with a proof that every rank-sized reflection generating set fails. Neither exists here; no finite obstruction supplied.

322517.title: The norm-one btt obstruction for intrinsically n-approximable distance functions
322517.statement:
Let $G$ be a computable connected graph whose distance function is intrinsically $n$-approximable from above, where $n>0$. A function is **$n$-approximable from above** if it has an approximation from above with at most $n$ changes at each input. For computable functions $f$ and $g$, write $f
ot
ot
eg?_{1\text{-}{\texttt{btt}}}g$? **Norm-one btt obstruction conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ which is $n$-approximable from above such that, for every computable graph $H\cong G$ with distance function $d_H$, $d_H\not\equiv_{1\text{-}{\texttt{btt}}} f$. This would establish that norm $2$ is intrinsically necessary in the btt-reductions between such distance functions and the functions they encode, rather than merely an artifact of the known constructions. The conjecture is presented as an open question in the source.
322517.ordinary_attempt: Norm-one diagonalization would have to defeat all computable copies H and all one-query reductions simultaneously. Merely encoding a chosen function by attaching graph gadgets proves no avoidance property.
322517.remaining_gap: Need a computable approximation with at most n downward changes per input, plus diagonal requirements uniformly across all copies; no priority construction supplied. Literal record contains corrupted reduction notation.

319799.title: Ackerman's linear extremal conjecture for forbidden circle-graph matchings
319799.statement: A **geometric graph** is a graph drawn in the plane with vertices represented by points and edges as straight-line segments. A **circle graph** $F$ is the intersection graph of chords on a circle. A matching in a geometric graph has an intersection graph whose vertices correspond to the matching edges, with adjacency when the corresponding edges cross. **Ackerman's linear extremal conjecture for forbidden circle-graph matchings.** For any circle graph $F$ on $k$ vertices, there exists a constant $c_k$ such that every $n$-vertex geometric graph that does not contain a matching whose intersection graph is $F$ contains at most $c_kn$ edges. This extends the paper's established linear bound for the relevant three-vertex case and would give a uniform linear extremal bound for every fixed circle graph. The general assertion is presented as a conjecture and no resolution is supplied here.

319799.ordinary_attempt: A single finite dense geometric graph cannot contradict existence of c_k. Taking F complete recovers the pairwise crossing extremal subproblem. Source matching means disjoint endpoints with prescribed crossings, not arbitrary edge copies.
319799.remaining_gap: Need an unbounded-density F-avoiding family for one fixed circle graph, or a full uniform linear bound. Neither route available.

320610.title: Finiteness conjecture for non-singular unsatisfiable hitting clause-sets
320610.statement:
A clause-set is **hitting** if every two distinct clauses $C,C'$ clash in at least one variable, that is, $\lvert C\cap\overline{C'}\rvert\geq 1$. A clause-set is **non-singular** in the sense used in the paper, and its **deficiency** is denoted by $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Two clause-sets have the same isomorphism type when they are isomorphic under the relevant variable and clause structure.

**Finiteness conjecture.** For every deficiency $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there are only finitely many isomorphism types of non-singular unsatisfiable hitting clause-sets.

This is presented as the main conjecture motivating the classification of minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets by deficiency, especially the classification of unsatisfiable hitting clause-sets. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
320610.review_depth: v1/v2/v3 Conjecture 6.1; v3 known k<=3 scope
320610.ordinary_attempt: Hitting unsatisfiability gives a partition of the Boolean cube into clause-falsifying subcubes. The identity sum_C 2^(-|C|)=1 does not bound variables at fixed deficiency. Non-singularity rules out the simplest repeatedly split-clause construction.
320610.remaining_gap: Need an explicit fixed-deficiency infinite non-singular family, or a bound on n(F) in terms of c(F)-n(F). No such bound/construction proved.

320804.title: The product conjecture for finite transitive sets
320804.statement:
Let $X\subset\mathbb R^m$ be a finite transitive set. A finite set $Y\subset\mathbb R^d$ is **$k$-Ramsey for $X$** if every $k$-colouring of $Y$ contains a monochromatic subset congruent to $X$. For a positive integer $n$, regard $X^n$ as a subset of $\mathbb R^{mn}$, and call a scalar multiple of it a **scaling** of $X^n$.

**Product conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that some scaling of $X^n$ is $k$-Ramsey for $X$.

This is a stronger formulation of the transitive-set characterization: it would immediately imply the “if” direction. It abstracts the product-and-scaling constructions used in known proofs that particular sets are Ramsey. The paper states that it is equivalent to the main transitive-set conjecture, but does not establish it.
320804.review_depth: v1 Conjecture B and product/group-action equivalences
320804.ordinary_attempt: Hales-Jewett supplies a monochromatic combinatorial line but its number of moving coordinates depends on the colouring. Turning that into the required congruent unscaled X forces a scaling choice with the wrong quantifier order.
320804.remaining_gap: Need predetermined scale and n for every colouring, not scale selected after seeing a monochromatic line. Source equivalences alone are no new proof.

320805.title: The block-permutation conjecture
320805.statement:
For positive integers $m$ and $n$, let $[m]=\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and let $[m]^n$ denote the words of length $n$ over $[m]$. A **block permutation set** in $[m]^n$ is obtained by choosing pairwise disjoint blocks $I_1,\ldots,I_m\subset[n]$, fixing all coordinates outside their union, and taking all words obtained by assigning a permutation of $1,\ldots,m$ to the blocks. Its **degree** is $\sum_{j=1}^m|I_j|$.

**Block-permutation conjecture.** For every pair of positive integers $m$ and $k$, there exist positive integers $n$ and $d$ such that every $k$-colouring of $[m]^n$ contains a block permutation set of degree $d$.

This is the fixed-block-size Hales--Jewett-type formulation arising from the group-action conjecture. It asks for a monochromatic family containing all permutations of the alphabet across prescribed blocks; the paper presents it as a conjectural combinatorial reformulation.
320805.review_depth: v1 Conjecture D, block definition, Proposition 2.2
320805.ordinary_attempt: Ordinary Hales-Jewett drops the fixed positive degree d; that weakening is explicitly proved in the source. Empty individual blocks are allowed, but all blocks empty would have degree zero and cannot solve the assertion.
320805.remaining_gap: Need d selected before the colouring and guaranteed positive. No colour-independent block-degree mechanism.

320911.title: Polar-dual Neumann eigenvalue sum conjecture for convex domains
320911.statement:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded convex domain containing the origin. Write $\mu_j$ for its Neumann Laplace eigenvalues, $V$ for volume, $I$ for the moment of inertia, and $\Omega^\circ$ for the polar dual of $\Omega$, defined by

$$
\Omega^\circ=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:x\cdot y<1\text{ for all }y\in\overline{\Omega}\}.
$$

**Polar-dual Neumann eigenvalue sum conjecture.** The scale-invariant quantity

$$
\left.(\mu_2+\dots+\mu_n)V^{2/d}\right|_\Omega\left.\frac{V^{1+2/d}}{I}\right|_{\Omega^\circ}
$$

is maximal when $\Omega$ is a ball, for each $n\geq2$.
This conjecture proposes the maximizer for the Neumann analogue of a bounded polar-dual eigenvalue expression; the corresponding Dirichlet quantity is bounded above using John’s ellipsoid theorem, but the maximizing statement for general convex domains is presented as an open problem.
320911.review_depth: v1 Conjecture 4.1 and following two-dimensional comparison
320911.ordinary_attempt: Affine ellipsoid/transplantation bounds address source special families. They do not compare all convex bodies, all dimensions and all partial Neumann sums. Translating the origin also changes the polar body.
320911.remaining_gap: Need rigorous spectral inequalities for general convex domains; no exact analytic witness or universal comparison produced.

318150.title: Sun's Lucas and mixed Fibonacci–Lucas representation conjectures
318150.statement: Let $F_n$ and $L_n$ denote the Fibonacci and Lucas sequences, respectively. A sequence term is **positive** when its value is positive, and a term is **odd** when it is not divisible by $2$. **Sun's Lucas and mixed Fibonacci–Lucas conjectures.** (i) Every integer $n>4$ can be written as the sum of an odd prime, an odd Lucas number, and a positive Lucas number. For $k=2,3$, every integer $n>4$ can be written as $p+L_s+L_t^k$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $s,t\geqslant0$, and $L_s$ or $L_t$ is odd. (ii) Every integer $n>4$ can be written as the sum of an odd prime, a positive Fibonacci number, and twice a positive Fibonacci number, or half of a positive Fibonacci number. Also, every integer $n>4$ can be written as the sum of an odd prime, twice a positive Fibonacci number, and the square of a positive Fibonacci number. (iii) Every integer $n>4$ can be written as $p+F_s+L_t$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $s>0$, and $F_s$ or $L_t$ is odd. The source reports extensive computational checks, but these assertions remain open.
318150.review_depth: v1/v2/v3 conjecture/status passages; latest inspected text includes unrelated Pell counterexamples
318150.ordinary_attempt: A finite modular obstruction might refute one representation clause, but Fibonacci/Lucas parity alone leaves admissible residues. Printed counterexamples to Pell variants concern different sequences and coefficients.
318150.remaining_gap: No covering congruence or exact unrepresentable integer for the stated Lucas/Fibonacci clauses. No uniform prime-representation proof.

318395.title: Linear-equations conjecture for d-refined alternating sign matrix enumeration
318395.statement:
For $1\le d<n$ and $1\le i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_d\le n$, let $A_{n,i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d}$ be the number of monotone triangles of order $n-d$ whose bottom row is the increasing arrangement of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d\}$; when $d=n$, set $A_{n,1,2,\ldots,n}=1$. Extend these values to an array $(\hat{A}_{n,i_1,\ldots,i_d})_{1\le i_1,\ldots,i_d\le n}$.

**Linear-equations conjecture.** The extension can be chosen so that, for $1\le i_1,i_2,\ldots,i_d\le n$,

$$
\hat{A}_{n,i_1,\ldots,i_d}=(-1)^{nd}\sum_{j_1=i_1}^n\cdots\sum_{j_d=i_d}^n(-1)^{j_1+\cdots+j_d}\prod_{r=1}^d\binom{2n-i_r-d}{j_r-i_r}\hat{A}_{n,j_d,\ldots,j_2,j_1}.
$$

This extends the linear relations for doubly refined enumeration to arbitrary refinement degree $d$. The source presents it as conjectural; no resolution evidence is supplied.
318395.review_depth: v1/v2 Conjecture 5 and Proposition 8; Fischer 0907.0401 Theorem 1 and Section 6 equation (6.1); 1008.0527 coefficient discussion
318395.ordinary_attempt: Complete published reduction: Fischer Theorem 1 identifies the binomial-basis coefficients with the monotone-trapezoid counts at increasing indices. Reflect/translate the bottom row of alpha(n;k_1,...,k_n), then change binomial bases. Section 6 gives exactly the reversed-index signed product-binomial relation (6.1) for all indices, explicitly identifying it as Fischer-Romik Conjecture 5. Coefficients provide the extension.
318395.remaining_gap: No discovery credit: exact general linear-equations conjecture is publicly proved. Uniqueness conjectures are different questions, not this reservation.

317029.title: The existence conjecture for $k$-symmetric permutations
317029.statement: Let $4\mathfrak{S}_n4$ be the symmetric group on $n$ symbols. For $4\tau\in\mathfrak{S}_k4$ and $4\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_n4$, let $4\mathbf{X}^{\tau}(\sigma)4$ count the occurrences of the pattern $4\tau4$ in $4\sigma4$. Call $4\sigma4$ **$k$-symmetric** when $4\mathbf{X}^{\tau}(\sigma)=\mathbf{X}^{\tau'}(\sigma)4$ for all $4\tau,\tau'\in\mathfrak{S}_k4$. Let $4\operatorname{alldiv}_k(n)4$ mean that $4\operatorname{div}_j(n)4$ holds for every $4j=1,\ldots,k4$, where $4\operatorname{div}_j(n)4$ means $4j!\mid\binom{n}{j}4$. **Existence conjecture for symmetric permutations.** If $4\operatorname{alldiv}_k(n)4$, then there exists a $k$-symmetric permutation on $n$ symbols. The divisibility condition is necessary because each of the $4k!4$ patterns must occur equally often. The conjecture asks whether this necessary condition is sufficient; the paper notes that the first nontrivial unresolved search in the case $4k=44$ occurs at $4n=644$.
317029.review_depth: v1 definitions, Conjecture 1, divisibility discussion; Kral-Pikhurko journal Theorem 3 and proof opening
317029.ordinary_attempt: Tried inversion/pattern moment constraints and finite-to-limit rigidity. Uniform k-pattern counts imply lower pattern uniformity by double-counting extensions. This supplies the printed divisibility restrictions, not sufficiency. Theorem 3 for permutons uses independent samples: repeated selection of a finite permutation cell introduces collision terms, so finite exact 4-symmetry does not give a 4-symmetric permuton.
317029.remaining_gap: Need a finite identity forcing a contradiction at an admissible n (e.g. n=64,k=4), or a full construction for every admissible pair. No identity/witness. The record status quotation concerns Graham asymptotic questions, not Conjecture 1.

317510.title: The level partial-field universality conjecture
317510.statement:
Let ${\mathbb{P}}$ be a partial field, and let ${\cal M}$ be a class of matroids. Say that ${\mathbb{P}}$ is ${\cal M}$-universal if, for every partial field ${\mathbb{P}}'$ such that every matroid in ${\cal M}$ is ${\mathbb{P}}'$-representable, there exists a homomorphism ${\mathbb{P}}\rightarrow {\mathbb{P}}'$. A partial field is **level** if it is obtained as the universal partial field associated with the class of matroids representable over another partial field. **Level partial-field universality conjecture.** Let ${\cal M}$ be the set of all ${\mathbb{P}}$-representable matroids, where ${\mathbb{P}}$ is a level partial field. Then ${\mathbb{P}}$ is ${\cal M}$-universal.

This conjecture asks whether every level partial field is universal for precisely the class of matroids it represents. The source presents it as an open question in the discussion of universal and level partial fields.

317510.ordinary_attempt: The word level does not make the required homomorphism tautological: the class used to build the level field and the class of all its represented matroids require comparison. Counting homomorphisms to GF(5) does not construct one to every eligible target partial field.
317510.remaining_gap: Need the universal property with exact lift/class definitions. Hydra-k omissions are explicitly noted by source. No construction or obstruction.

317936.title: The Lefschetz condition conjecture for Braden–MacPherson sheaves
317936.statement:
Let $w\in{\widehat{\mathcal W}}$ and suppose that $\operatorname{char} K>N(w)$. For every $x\le w$, let

$$
i_x\colon\overline{\mathcal B}(w)_x\to\overline{\mathcal B}(w)^x
$$

be the indicated map between the costalk and stalk of the reduced Braden–MacPherson sheaf. Recall that a map $f\colon A\to B$ of graded free $K[t]$-modules satisfies the Lefschetz condition with center $l\in\mathbb Z$ if multiplication by $t^n$ induces an isomorphism

$$
(\operatorname{coker}f)_{\{l-n\}}\stackrel{\sim}{\to}(\operatorname{coker}f)_{\{l+n\}}
$$

for every $n\ge1$. **The Lefschetz condition conjecture.** For all $x\le w$, the map $i_x$ satisfies the Lefschetz condition with center $l(w)$. This conjecture proposes a Hard Lefschetz-type symmetry for the stalk–costalk maps of Braden–MacPherson sheaves in characteristic greater than $N(w)$. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

316289.title: The constraining conjecture for minimal simply three-edge-connected graphs
316289.statement:
Let $\vec{G}$ be a minimal simply three edge connected, totally cyclic directed graph, and let $G$ be its underlying graph. A twisted graph has the form $T=(\vec{G},G,<,A)$, where $<$ is a total order on the edges and $A$ is the associated set of constraints; it is constraining when, for some compatible angle vector, the corresponding strict system is insoluble while the associated homogeneous system has a nontrivial solution.

**Constraining conjecture.** For every minimal simply three edge connected, totally cyclic directed graph $\vec{G}$, there is a total order $<$ and a constraining twisted graph $T=(\vec{G},G,<,A)$.

The paper presents this as a weaker consequence of the preceding conjectures, via its twistability lemma. It remains an open proposed sufficient condition for constructing the relevant line arrangements.

379793.title: Quantum determinant–permanent reciprocity conjecture
379793.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Sing}_{n,q}^{\mathrm{per}}$ and $\operatorname{Sing}_{n,q}$ be the singular sets for the quantum permanent and quantum determinant, respectively. For $\lambda\in{\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_n}^{\mathrm{dom}}$, let $\lambda'$ denote the transposed diagram, and let $m_q^\lambda(\alpha)_{\mathrm{per}}$ and $m_q^\lambda(\alpha)$ be the corresponding multiplicities. **Quantum determinant–permanent reciprocity conjecture.** (1) If $\alpha(q)\in\operatorname{Sing}_{n,q}^{\mathrm{per}}$, then $\alpha(q^{-1})\in\operatorname{Sing}_{n,q}$. (2) The map

$$
\operatorname{Sing}_{n,q}^{\mathrm{per}}\ni\alpha(q)\longmapsto\alpha(q^{-1})\in\operatorname{Sing}_{n,q}
$$

is bijective. (3) For every $\alpha(q)\in\operatorname{Sing}_{n,q}^{\mathrm{per}}$ and every $\lambda\in{\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_n}^{\mathrm{dom}}$,

$$
m_q^\lambda(\alpha(q))_{\mathrm{per}}=m_q^{\lambda'}(\alpha(q^{-1})).
$$

This expresses a mirror symmetry under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ and transposition of diagrams. The source notes that it is true when $q=1$, but leaves the general case conjectural.

379797.title: Span-intersection conjecture for upper and lower roots
379797.statement:
Let $W$ be a finite Coxeter group of rank $n$, let $c$ be a Coxeter element, and let $(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k,\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_{n-k})$ be a $c$-cluster, where the $\alpha_i$ are its lower roots and the $\beta_i$ are its upper roots. Let $\phi_c$ be the recursively defined map on roots, and write $\beta_i^{\perp}$ for the hyperplane orthogonal to $\beta_i$. **Span-intersection conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb{R}}(\phi_c^{-1}(\alpha_1),\ldots,\phi_c^{-1}(\alpha_k))=\beta_1^{\perp}\cap\cdots\cap\beta_{n-k}^{\perp}.
$$

The two spaces have the same dimension, and the required orthogonality has been verified computationally for all Coxeter elements in Coxeter groups of rank at most $7$; proving the equality would remove the recursive map from the description of the associated noncrossing subspace.

379977.title: Orbit-closure classification of square-free words in odd-difference progressions
379977.statement:
Let ${\bf f}=f_0f_1f_2\cdots$ be a paperfolding word over $\{1,4\}$, and define ${\bf v}=v_0v_1v_2\cdots$ by

$$
v_{4n}=2,\qquad v_{4n+2}=3,\qquad v_{2n+1}=f_{2n+1}
$$

for all $n\geq 0$, with the even-position symbols of ${\bf f}$ recoded as $2$ and $3$. The **orbit closure** of a word is the set of infinite words obtained as limits of shifts of that word. **The orbit-closure classification conjecture.** Every infinite word over a 4-letter alphabet that avoids squares in arithmetic progressions of odd difference belongs to the orbit closure of one of the words ${\bf v}$ constructed above. There are uncountably many such words ${\bf v}$ arising from paperfolding words, and the preceding theorem shows that they avoid squares in arithmetic progressions of odd difference; the conjecture asserts that these constructions account for all infinite examples, but no resolution is supplied in the source.

379982.title: Factor-criticality conjecture for K_{1,5}-free 3-vertex-critical graphs
379982.statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. It is **factor-critical** if, for every vertex $v\in V(G)$, the graph $G-v$ has a perfect matching. The graph $G$ is **$K_{1,5}$-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,5}$, and it is **3-vertex-critical** if $\gamma(G-v)<\gamma(G)=3$ for every vertex $v\in V(G)$, where $\gamma(G)$ is the domination number. Let $G$ also be 2-connected, have odd order, and satisfy $\delta(G)\geq 3$. **Factor-criticality conjecture.** Then $G$ is factor-critical. This conjecture concerns when domination-critical graphs necessarily have the matching property that every vertex deletion leaves a perfect matching. Earlier results establish factor-criticality under the stronger assumption that the graph is $K_{1,4}$-free, while the stated $K_{1,5}$-free case is presented as an open conjecture.

378963.title: Structural conjecture for sumsets bounded by a fixed multiple of the set size
378963.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a real number satisfying

$$
3<\alpha<3+\frac{1}{3},
$$

and let $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ be finite. Write $2A=A+A=\{a+a':a,a'\in A\}$ and set $b=|2A|-3|A|+3$. An **arithmetic progression** is a finite set of equally spaced integers, and a **bi-progression** is the structured object used in the source's additive-combinatorial results.

**Structural conjecture.** There exists a $K\in\mathbb N$ such that for every finite set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ with $|A|>K$, if

$$
3|A|-3\leqslant |2A|=3|A|-3+b\leqslant\alpha|A|,
$$

then $A$ is either a subset of an arithmetic progression of length at most $2|A|-1+2b$ or a subset of a bi-progression of length at most $|A|+b$.

The source presents this as a weaker version of its main conjecture, intended to be easier to prove and useful for improving a stated corollary. Its status evidence says that the paper's main theorem confirms only a weak version, so the conjecture remained unresolved there.

Their ratio tends to 10/3, so for any fixed alpha<10/3 they eventually fail the hypothesis and cannot refute the existence of K. Small finite exceptions also do not refute an eventual statement.
378963.remaining_gap: Need an unbounded family with one fixed alpha<10/3 avoiding both prescribed progression covers. Source proves only a small-epsilon interval; no extension to entire interval.

379094.title: The extremal configuration conjecture for the $pi$-pebbling function
379094.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $p_i$ denote the pebbling demand associated with vertex $i$, and let $pi^{t}(G)=k$. A configuration assigns $c_i$ pebbles to each vertex, and it is **non-$t$-solvable** if it cannot be pebbled to a configuration satisfying the relevant $t$-pebbling requirement. For the standard price function, let $d$ be the diameter of $G$.

**Extremal configuration conjecture.** There exists a non-$t$-solvable configuration $C$ of $k-1$ pebbles on $G$ such that, for every vertex $i$, $c_i$ is either $0$ or $p_i-1$, except possibly at one vertex $r$. For the standard price function, $r$ should have another vertex $s$ at distance $d$ from it, and there should be a shortest path from $r$ to such an $s$ containing no pebbles other than those on $r$.

This conjecture proposes a generalization of the Cover Pebbling Theorem to non-positive weight functions. Establishing such a description of an extremal configuration would make it easier to calculate the $pi$-pebbling function for graphs such as wheels.

Moving a price packet consumes p_i-1 pebbles, so legal moves cannot be used to preserve the extremal total while concentrating. Fixed-target potentials certify unsolvability but do not prove all configurations of k pebbles solvable. Source complete/path/star formulas already realize its concentration recipes.

379147.title: Sundaram–Welker vanishing conjecture for polynomial root-multiplicity strata
379147.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$, let $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_t)\vdash n$ be a number partition, and let $\Sigma_\lambda^{S^2}$ be the one-point compactification of the space of monic degree-$n$ complex polynomials whose roots can be partitioned into sets of sizes $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_t$, with equal roots within each set. Write $l(\lambda)=t$ and let $\tilde\beta_i(\Sigma_\lambda^{S^2},{\mathbb Q})$ denote its reduced rational Betti numbers.

**Sundaram–Welker's conjecture.** For every number partition $\lambda$,

$$
\tilde\beta_i(\Sigma_\lambda^{S^2},{\mathbb Q})=0
$$

unless $i=2l(\lambda)$.

This predicts concentration of the reduced rational homology of these root-multiplicity strata in a single degree; the supplied text attributes the conjecture to Sundaram and Welker but gives no resolution status.
